title: Fully integrated continuous-variable quantum key distribution with composable security over 100 km
authors: Yankai Xu, Xinhang Li, Tao Wang, Jisheng Dai, Xueqin Jiang, Yuyao Guo, Peng Huang, Linjie Zhou, Guihua Zeng
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) guarantees information-theoretic security by the laws of physics, but deployment at scale requires compact, manufacturable photonic terminals. Continuous-variable QKD (CV-QKD) is well suited for this transition through telecom-compatible, room-temperature coherent detection. However, unifying full on-chip core terminal integration, room-temperature operation, high loss tolerance, and composable end-to-end security in long-distance QKD remains a key bottleneck. Here we report a fully integrated CV-QKD platform in which two hybrid III--V/Si$_3$N$_4$ integrated lasers, a silicon transmitter, and a silicon coherent receiver implement the core terminal functions, operating with a local local oscillator (LLO) over fibre links of 25--150 km. A Bayesian machine-learning algorithm maintains robust phase lock throughout the long records required for composable security, consistently outperforming the conventional unscented Kalman filter, while rate-matched multidimensional reconciliation approaches the Shannon limit. The system certifies a composable finite-size secret-key rate of 29.3 kbps at 100 km from a 140-billion-symbol block, with 12.9 kbps at 125 km under finite-size analysis and 9.17 kbps at 150 km under asymptotic analysis. By establishing the longest finite-size and asymptotic reaches and the highest secret-key rate per symbol reported for integrated CV-QKD, this work advances the development of practical chip-based quantum networks.
summary: This paper reports a fully integrated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution (CV-QKD) platform capable of operating over long distances (up to 150 km) using chip-scale photonics. By combining advanced components, a machine-learning phase-locking algorithm, and rate-matched reconciliation, the authors achieved high secret-key rates while maintaining composable security. This work significantly advances the feasibility of practical, chip-based quantum networks.
main_problem: Scaling Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) to network levels requires compact, manufacturable photonic terminals while maintaining high security over long distances.
main_result: The authors demonstrated a fully integrated CV-QKD platform achieving a certified secret-key rate of 29.3 kbps at 100 km, establishing records for reach and rate in integrated chip-based QKD.
method: The system uses a co-designed digital chain involving a Bayesian machine-learning algorithm for phase lock and rate-matched multidimensional reconciliation for key extraction.
model_or_system: The platform integrates two hybrid III-V/Si3N4 lasers, a silicon transmitter, and a silicon coherent receiver, operating over fiber links up to 150 km using a Local Local Oscillator (LLO).
key_observables: Composable finite-size secret-key rate (e.g., 29.3 kbps at 100 km), excess noise ($\xi$), and intrinsic laser linewidths (10 and 30 Hz).
important_parameters: Long-distance transmission (100-150 km), finite-size security analysis ($\epsilon \leq 6 	imes 2^{-32}$), and the Shannon limit approach.
main_assumptions: The security analysis relies on a composable finite-size framework, and the system performance is limited by residual phase noise ($\xi_{RPN}$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the integrated platform components, the end-to-end workflow from signal generation to key extraction, and the measured excess noise ($\xi$) across various distances.
paper_structure: The paper details the integrated hardware platform, analyzes noise sources (RIN, preparation, phase noise), presents the advanced phase-locking and reconciliation algorithms, and finally reports the key rate performance across increasing distances.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the engineering bottleneck of quantum networking by demonstrating a fully integrated, chip-scale solution for CV-QKD, which is crucial for realizing practical quantum internet infrastructure.
